ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A large cube is made from 64 small cubes. The 5 visible faces of the large cube are green, the bottom face is red. How many of the small cubes have 3 green faces?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large cube assembled from small cubes, and the visible faces are divided into 4×4 small grids, matching the structure in which each edge has 4 small cubes. Reasoning: Because the large cube is composed of 64 small cubes, 64=4×4×4, so it is a 4-by-4-by-4 large cube. A small cube can have 3 outer surfaces colored only when it is at a corner of the large cube. The large cube has 8 corners in total. The problem states that 5 visible faces are green and the bottom face is red; therefore, each of the 4 corner small cubes at the bottom has 2 green faces and 1 red face, which does not satisfy having 3 green faces. The 3 outer surfaces that the 4 corner small cubes at the top touch are all green, so each has 3 green faces. Therefore, the number of small cubes with 3 green faces is 4.

method.method_draft: Identify the large cube as a 4-by-4-by-4 cube because it is made from 64 small cubes. A small cube can have 3 painted outer faces only if it is a corner cube. There are 8 corner cubes total. The 4 bottom corner cubes each include the bottom face, which is red, so they have only 2 green faces and 1 red face. The 4 top corner cubes touch only green faces, so they each have 3 green faces. Answer: 4.

method.method_draft: Model the cube by layers. Since 64 = 4^3, each edge has 4 small cubes. To have 3 green faces, a small cube must lie on three green boundary faces. In the vertical direction, the only green horizontal face is the top face, because the bottom is red. So the cube must be in the top layer. Within the top layer, it must also lie on two side boundary faces, which happens only at the four corner positions of the top 4-by-4 square. Therefore there are 4 such cubes.
